author.name: Rudyard Kipling
author.heading: About Rudyard Kipling
author.bio: Rudyard Kipling wrote fiction and verse, including The Jungle Book and Kim. His cousin Stanley Baldwin carried this sharp comparison into a political attack on newspaper proprietors; the family testimony is central to the attribution.

cite.sourceCitation: Baldwin, Stanley. Queen’s Hall speech, March 17, 1931, contemporary reports documented by Quote Investigator. Kipling attribution: Arthur W. Baldwin, “The Unfading Genius of Rudyard Kipling,” The Kipling Journal 38, no. 180 (December 1971): 6.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘Power without responsibility—the prerogative of the harlot throughout the ages’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

copyAttribution: Credibly attributed to Rudyard Kipling on Arthur W. Baldwin’s testimony; publicly used by Stanley Baldwin in his Queen’s Hall speech, 17 March 1931.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Baldwin was attacking the newspapers of Lords Rothermere and Beaverbrook as instruments of their proprietors’ changing personal policies. The phrase made their influence sound detached from the obligations of elected office.

Arthur Baldwin later explained that Kipling had first used the analogy in private conversation with Beaverbrook and permitted his cousin to borrow it. That account supports Kipling’s credit without turning the later recollection into contemporary proof of the private exchange.
